name: BEND run guide correction: lxml, h5py and pysam missing from requirements.txt (upstream)
description: The BEND run guide installed from requirements.txt, which until commit 58ad410 lacked three packages the download and embedding scripts import.

attributes.previous_value:
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
python scripts/download_bend.py
attributes.rationale: Upstream problem. scripts/download_bend.py at ac6e80c parses the share listing with BeautifulSoup(..., "lxml"), and scripts/precompute_embeddings.py needs h5py and pysam, but requirements.txt at ac6e80c lists none of the three, so the guide's install step left the download failing with bs4.FeatureNotFound. Reported by a third party as BEND issue #53 in April 2024, not by Rewire. Rewire's first correction (rewire-benchmarks#71, 2026-11-17) installed lxml, h5py and pysam explicitly. Commit 58ad410 added all three to requirements.txt, so the guide pinned to 58ad410 installs from requirements.txt alone. The data download that shared this step moved to its own step (see the companion claim on steps.2.shell).
attributes.upstream_response: No maintainer reply on issue #53, which was still open on 2026-11-19. Commit 58ad410 (PR #79, merged 2026-11-18) added h5py, pysam and lxml to requirements.txt, with numpy<2 and setuptools<81; the PR says it "adds dependencies needed by the tested workflow".

name: BEND run guide correction: dead checkpoint links and folder names (upstream, reported by Rewire, fixed)
description: The BEND baseline checkpoints could not be downloaded through the repository's own code until commit 58ad410, and the configuration named folders the share did not have.

attributes.previous_value: This is the README example verbatim; it computes two models and two tasks. Embeddings are stored as Webdataset tar.gz shards; the next step uses the gene-finding subset.
attributes.value: Adapted from the README example, with the task list narrowed to gene_finding because only those inputs are fetched. When pretrained_models/convnet/ or pretrained_models/awd_lstm/ is missing, ConvNetEmbedder and AWDLSTMEmbedder download the checkpoints with wget from ERDA share aNQa0Oz2lY. The resnetlm configuration loads pretrained_models/convnet, which the maintainer confirmed holds the paper's dilated ResNet; the resnetlm folder on the share is empty. To fetch the checkpoints ahead of time, call bend.utils.download.download_model('convnet', destination_dir='./pretrained_models/convnet/') and the same for 'awd_lstm'. With its default destination_dir the function writes the files directly into ./pretrained_models/, where the configuration does not look.
attributes.rationale: Upstream problem, reported by Rewire. At ac6e80c, download_model in bend/utils/download.py fetched from ERDA share dbQM0pgSlM and the README linked share eXAmVvbRSW; both returned 403 on 2026-11-17. ConvNetEmbedder and AWDLSTMEmbedder call download_model when pretrained_models/resnetlm/ or pretrained_models/awdlstm/ is missing, and os.system ignored the failed wget, so the guide's precompute step would have failed later, at from_pretrained. The files were in data share f6hdp1zTzh under pretrained_models/convnet/ and pretrained_models/awd_lstm/, not the folder names conf/embedding/embed.yaml used. Rewire's first correction (rewire-benchmarks#71, 2026-11-17) fetched the checkpoints with curl into the configured folder names. Commit 58ad410 moved download_model, the README and scripts/download_bend.py to share aNQa0Oz2lY, pointed resnetlm at pretrained_models/convnet/ and awdlstm at pretrained_models/awd_lstm/, and made a failed wget raise. With that, the precompute command downloads the checkpoints itself and the curl loop was dropped. HEAD requests on 2026-11-19 returned 200 under https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/aNQa0Oz2lY/pretrained_models/ for convnet/config.json, convnet/pytorch_model.bin (79,177,173 bytes) and awd_lstm/pytorch_model.bin (87,174,249 bytes), and 404 for resnetlm/config.json. Pinning the guide to 58ad410 is recorded in the companion claim on run_recipes.0.version.
attributes.upstream_response: Fixed by the maintainer in PR #79, merged 2026-11-18 as commit 58ad410; issue closed the same day. Maintainer's reply on 2026-11-18: "Thank you for letting us know and identifying the old share and directory mismatch. The fix should be on main now. However, the pretrained_models/resnetlm directory is still empty. It appears there has been a duplication and naming mismatch at some point and that the (Dilated) ResNet from the paper is actually in the folder pretrained_models/convnet. I apologise for the confusion. I have tested the automatic download as well as the download script and they both appear to work now." PR #79 says the full benchmark and GPU execution were not tested.

name: BEND run guide correction: downloaded the whole 7.25 GB share for one task (ours)
description: Rewire's BEND run guide downloaded every BEND task's data to run gene finding, which needs about half of it.

attributes.previous_value:
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
python scripts/download_bend.py
attributes.value:
S=https://sid.erda.dk/share_redirect/aNQa0Oz2lY
mkdir -p data/genomes data/gene_finding
for f in GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.fai; do
  curl -fL -o "data/genomes/$f" "$S/data/genomes/$f"
done
for f in gene_finding.bed gene_finding.hdf5; do
  curl -fL -o "data/gene_finding/$f" "$S/data/gene_finding/$f"
done
attributes.rationale: Rewire's own error, not an upstream one. The guide ran python scripts/download_bend.py, which fetches the whole ERDA share: 7,251,859,341 bytes in the f6hdp1zTzh listing on 2026-11-17. Gene finding reads only data/genomes/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa and data/gene_finding/gene_finding.{bed,hdf5} (conf/embedding/embed.yaml lines 106-109). With the .fai index those are 3,509,054,493 bytes, from HEAD requests on share aNQa0Oz2lY on 2026-11-19. GRCh37.no-chr.fa (3,199,905,630 bytes) is read only by chromatin accessibility (line 128). The guide now fetches the four files with curl, and the precompute step names task=gene_finding alone, since the enhancer_annotation files are no longer fetched. Not reported upstream: download_bend.py downloading everything is the documented behaviour.
